<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 700 450" width="700" height="450">
  <!-- Background -->
  <rect width="100%" height="100%" fill="white"/>

  <!-- Define styles for Times New Roman math font -->
  <style>
    .math {
      font-family: "Times New Roman", Times, serif;
      font-style: italic;
      font-size: 18px;
    }
    .text {
      font-family: Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif;
      font-size: 16px;
    }
    .vector {
      font-family: "Times New Roman", Times, serif;
      font-style: italic;
      font-size: 18px;
    }
  </style>

  <!-- Parallelogram ABCD vertices:
       A(150, 320)
       B(300, 120)
       C(540, 120)
       D(390, 320)
       Vector AB = C - D = (150, 0)? Wait:
       A = (150, 320), B = (300, 120). Vector AB = (150, -200).
       D = (390, 320), C = (540, 120). Vector DC = (150, -200).
       Vector BC = C - B = (240, 0).
       Vector AD = D - A = (240, 0).
       Let's check CD = D - C = (390-540, 320-120) = (-150, 200).
       Given CD = b, so b is vector CD or vector DC? Usually vectors are named with arrow, here CD = b.
       CD goes from (540,120) to (390,320).
       CE extends CD such that CD : CE = 1 : 2.
       Since CD length is 150 (x) and 200 (y), CE length is twice, in the same direction.
       C = (540, 120), D = (390, 320).
       Vector CD = D - C = (-150, 200).
       So E = D + CD = (390-150, 320+200) = (240, 520) - wait, CE = 2 * CD.
       Let's check: C to D is vector b. CD = b.
       So D = C + b. E lies on CD produced such that CD : CE = 1 : 2.
       Since it's "CD produced", we go past D.
       Distance CE = 2 * CD, so DE = CD = b.
       Thus E = D + CD = (240, 520) - wait, let's use exact coordinates.
  -->

  <!-- Coordinate calculations:
       A = (180, 320)
       B = (330, 120)
       C = (570, 120)
       D = (420, 320)
       
       Check Parallelogram:
       AB = (150, -200)
       DC = (570-420, 120-320) = (150, -200). Correct.
       AD = (420-180, 320-320) = (240, 0). Length = 240.
       BC = (570-330, 120-120) = (240, 0). Length = 240.

       M is midpoint of AD:
       M = ((180+420)/2, (320+320)/2) = (300, 320).

       N on BC such that BN : BC = 1 : 4.
       BC goes from (330, 120) to (570, 120). Length = 240.
       BN = 1/4 of BC = 60.
       N = (330 + 60, 120) = (390, 120).
       Given BN = a. Since N is on BC and BN = 1/4 BC, vector BN = a.
       Vector BC = 4a.
       Since AD = BC, vector AD = 4a.
       Since M is midpoint of AD, AM = 2a.

       CD = D - C = (420-570, 320-120) = (-150, 200).
       CD = b.
       E lies on CD produced such that CD : CE = 1 : 2.
       So vector CE = 2 * vector CD = 2b.
       Since C = (570, 120), E = C + 2(CD) = (570 + 2(-150), 120 + 2(200)) = (570 - 300, 120 + 400) = (270, 520).
       Wait, let's verify if E(270, 520) is too high up. SVG height is 450.
       Let's rescale the figure so everything fits nicely within 700x450.
  -->

  <!-- Recalculated coordinates:
       A = (200, 280)
       B = (320, 100)
       C = (520, 100)
       D = (400, 280)

       Check vectors:
       AB = (120, -180)
       DC = (520-400, 100-280) = (120, -180). Correct.
       AD = (200, 0), length 200.
       BC = (200, 0), length 200.

       M = midpoint of AD = (300, 280).
       N on BC such that BN : BC = 1 : 4.
       BC length = 200. BN = 50.
       N = (320 + 50, 100) = (370, 100).
       BN = a.

       CD = D - C = (400-520, 280-100) = (-120, 180).
       CD = b.

       E lies on CD produced such that CD : CE = 1 : 2.
       This means C, D, E are collinear, D is between C and E, and CE = 2 CD.
       So DE = CD = b.
       E = D + CD = (400 - 120, 280 + 180) = (280, 460) - still a bit high (y=460 out of 450).
       Let's compress vertically.
  -->

  <!-- Final Coordinates:
       A = (200, 250)
       B = (300, 90)
       C = (500, 90)
       D = (400, 250)

       AB = (100, -160)
       DC = (500-400, 90-250) = (100, -160). Correct.
       AD = (200, 0).
       BC = (200, 0).

       M = midpoint of AD = (300, 250).
       N on BC, BN : BC = 1 : 4. BC length = 200, so BN = 50.
       N = (300 + 50, 90) = (350, 90).

       CD = D - C = (400-500, 250-90) = (-100, 160).
       CD = b.
       CE = 2 * CD = 2 * (-100, 160) = (-200, 320).
       E = C + CE = (500 - 200, 90 + 320) = (300, 410).
       Wait, y = 410 is well within height 450! Perfect.
  -->

  <!-- Lines of the parallelogram and extensions -->
  <!-- Extension line from C through D to E -->
  <line x1="500" y1="90" x2="280" y2="430" stroke="black" stroke-width="1.5" stroke-dasharray="6,4"/>

  <!-- BC line (extended slightly or just BC segment) -->
  <line x1="300" y1="90" x2="500" y2="90" stroke="black" stroke-width="1.5"/>

  <!-- AB line -->
  <line x1="200" y1="250" x2="300" y2="90" stroke="black" stroke-width="1.5"/>

  <!-- AD line -->
  <line x1="200" y1="250" x2="400" y2="250" stroke="black" stroke-width="1.5"/>

  <!-- CD line segment -->
  <line x1="400" y1="250" x2="500" y2="90" stroke="black" stroke-width="1.5"/>

  <!-- Additional construction lines for vectors -->
  <!-- AM -->
  <line x1="200" y1="250" x2="300" y2="250" stroke="black" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  <!-- BM -->
  <line x1="300" y1="90" x2="300" y2="250" stroke="black" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  <!-- BE -->
  <line x1="300" y1="90" x2="300" y2="410" stroke="black" stroke-width="1.5"/>

  <!-- Points -->
  <circle cx="200" cy="250" r="3" fill="black"/>
  <circle cx="300" cy="90" r="3" fill="black"/>
  <circle cx="500" cy="90" r="3" fill="black"/>
  <circle cx="400" cy="250" r="3" fill="black"/>
  <circle cx="300" cy="250" r="3" fill="black"/> <!-- M -->
  <circle cx="350" cy="90" r="3" fill="black"/>  <!-- N -->
  <circle cx="300" cy="410" r="3" fill="black"/>  <!-- E -->

  <!-- Labels -->
  <text x="180" y="260" class="math">A</text>
  <text x="285" y="80" class="math">B</text>
  <text x="510" y="90" class="math">C</text>
  <text x="410" y="265" class="math">D</text>
  <text x="295" y="275" class="math">M</text>
  <text x="350" y="75" class="math">N</text>
  <text x="270" y="415" class="math">E</text>

  <!-- Optional vector indicators or helper annotations if needed, keeping it clean -->
</svg>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 700 500" width="700" height="500">
  <!-- Background -->
  <rect width="100%" height="100%" fill="white"/>

  <!-- Styles -->
  <style>
    .math {
      font-family: "Times New Roman", Times, serif;
      font-style: italic;
      font-size: 18px;
    }
  </style>

  <!-- 
    Parallelogram ABCD coordinates:
    Let B = (250, 100)
    Let C = (550, 100)
    Let A = (130, 320)
    Let D = (430, 320)

    Check vectors:
    BC = (300, 0)
    AD = (300, 0)
    AB = D - C? No, AB = (120, 220) -> Let's verify:
    A(130, 320), B(250, 100) => AB = (120, -220)
    D(430, 320), C(550, 100) => DC = (-120, 220), so CD = (120, -220).
    Thus CD = AB as vectors! Perfect parallelogram.

    M is midpoint of AD:
    A = (130, 320), D = (430, 320) => M = (280, 320).

    N on BC such that BN : BC = 1 : 4.
    B = (250, 100), C = (550, 100). Length = 300.
    BN = 300 / 4 = 75.
    N = (250 + 75, 100) = (325, 100).
    Given BN = a.

    CD = b.
    CD vector = (120, -220).
    E lies on CD produced such that CD : CE = 1 : 2.
    Since C, D, E are collinear in that order, CE = 2 * CD.
    So DE = CD = b.
    D = (430, 320). CD vector is (120, -220).
    E = D + CD = (430 + 120, 320 - 220) = (550, 100). Wait!
    If E = (550, 100), that is point C! 
    Ah, let's re-read: "CD : CE = 1 : 2".
    That means distance CD is 1 unit, and distance CE is 2 units.
    Since E is on CD *produced*, C is at one end, D is in the middle, E is at the far end!
    So C to D is 1 unit, D to E is 1 unit (making CE = 2 units).
    Therefore, E = D + CD = D + (D - C) = 2D - C.
    Let's calculate E:
    D = (430, 320), C = (550, 100).
    CD vector = D - C = (430 - 550, 320 - 100) = (-120, 220).
    Wait! Earlier I had CD = (120, -220) going from C to D. 
    Let's be precise:
    C = (550, 100), D = (430, 320).
    Vector CD = D - C = (430 - 550, 320 - 100) = (-120, 220).
    Vector b = CD = (-120, 220).
    E lies on CD produced such that CD : CE = 1 : 2.
    Vector CE = 2 * vector CD = 2 * (-120, 220) = (-240, 440).
    E = C + CE = (550 - 240, 100 + 440) = (310, 540).
    y = 540 is outside height 500. Let's rescale the parallelogram.
  -->

  <!-- 
    Rescaled Coordinates:
    B = (280, 120)
    C = (520, 120)
    A = (160, 300)
    D = (400, 300)

    Check Parallelogram:
    AB = (120, -180)
    CD = D - C = (400 - 520, 300 - 120) = (-120, 180) = b.
    AD = (240, 0), length 240.
    BC = (240, 0), length 240.

    M = midpoint of AD = ( (160+400)/2, 300 ) = (280, 300).

    N on BC such that BN : BC = 1 : 4.
    BC length = 240. BN = 240 / 4 = 60.
    N = (280 + 60, 120) = (340, 120).
    BN = a.
    Vector BN = (60, 0) = a.

    CD = b = (-120, 180).
    E lies on CD produced such that CD : CE = 1 : 2.
    Vector CE = 2 * vector CD = 2 * (-120, 180) = (-240, 360).
    E = C + CE = (520 - 240, 120 + 360) = (280, 480).
    y = 480 fits nicely in height 500!
  -->

  <!-- Lines of the parallelogram -->
  <!-- AB -->
  <line x1="160" y1="300" x2="280" y2="120" stroke="black" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  <!-- BC -->
  <line x1="280" y1="120" x2="520" y2="120" stroke="black" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  <!-- AD -->
  <line x1="160" y1="300" x2="400" y2="300" stroke="black" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  <!-- CD and its extension to E -->
  <!-- C(520, 120) to D(400, 300), then produced to E(280, 480) -->
  <line x1="520" y1="120" x2="280" y2="480" stroke="black" stroke-width="1.5"/>

  <!-- Additional required lines for questions (AM, BM, BE) -->
  <!-- AM: from A(160, 300) to M(280, 300) - already part of AD, let's make sure it's clear -->
  <!-- BM: from B(280, 120) to M(280, 300) -->
  <line x1="280" y1="120" x2="280" y2="300" stroke="black" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  
  <!-- BE: from B(280, 120) to E(280, 480) -->
  <!-- Notice M(280, 300) lies on BE since x=280 for B, M, and E! -->
  <line x1="280" y1="300" x2="280" y2="480" stroke="black" stroke-width="1.5"/>

  <!-- Vertices and points -->
  <circle cx="160" cy="300" r="3" fill="black"/>
  <circle cx="280" cy="120" r="3" fill="black"/>
  <circle cx="520" cy="120" r="3" fill="black"/>
  <circle cx="400" cy="300" r="3" fill="black"/>
  <circle cx="280" cy="300" r="3" fill="black"/> <!-- M -->
  <circle cx="340" cy="120" r="3" fill="black"/> <!-- N -->
  <circle cx="280" cy="480" r="3" fill="black"/> <!-- E -->

  <!-- Labels -->
  <text x="140" y="305" class="math">A</text>
  <text x="265" y="110" class="math">B</text>
  <text x="530" y="125" class="math">C</text>
  <text x="415" y="315" class="math">D</text>
  <text x="290" y="315" class="math">M</text>
  <text x="335" y="105" class="math">N</text>
  <text x="260" y="485" class="math">E</text>

</svg>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 750 480" width="750" height="480">
  <!-- Background -->
  <rect width="100%" height="100%" fill="white"/>

  <!-- Styles -->
  <style>
    .math {
      font-family: "Times New Roman", Times, serif;
      font-style: italic;
      font-size: 18px;
    }
  </style>

  <!-- 
    Let's correctly place vertices so E is genuinely on CD produced (collinear with C and D).
    
    Parallelogram ABCD:
    A = (150, 280)
    B = (330, 100)
    C = (570, 100)
    D = (390, 280)

    Check vectors:
    BC = C - B = (240, 0)
    AD = D - A = (240, 0)
    AB = B - A = (180, -180)
    CD = D - C = (390 - 570, 280 - 100) = (-180, 180)
    Since CD = (-180, 180) and AB = (180, -180), AB = -CD, meaning AB is parallel to CD and equal in length. Perfect parallelogram.

    M is the midpoint of AD:
    A = (150, 280), D = (390, 280)
    M = ( (150+390)/2, 280 ) = (270, 280).

    N on BC such that BN : BC = 1 : 4.
    B = (330, 100), C = (570, 100). Length = 240.
    BN = 240 / 4 = 60.
    N = (330 + 60, 100) = (390, 100).

    CD = b = (-180, 180).
    E lies on CD produced such that CD : CE = 1 : 2.
    This means C, D, E are collinear, with D between C and E, and CE = 2 * CD (so DE = CD = b).
    Vector CE = 2 * vector CD = 2 * (-180, 180) = (-360, 360).
    E = C + CE = (570 - 360, 100 + 360) = (210, 460).
    y = 460 fits inside height 480.

    Let's check the line segment for BE:
    B = (330, 100), E = (210, 460).
    Vector BE = E - B = (210 - 330, 460 - 100) = (-120, 360).
    Line DE is the continuation of CD:
    C = (570, 100), D = (390, 280), E = (210, 460).
    Slope of CD = (280 - 100) / (390 - 570) = 180 / -180 = -1.
    Slope of DE = (460 - 280) / (210 - 390) = 180 / -180 = -1.
    Collinear and correctly placed!
  -->

  <!-- Parallelogram sides -->
  <!-- AB -->
  <line x1="150" y1="280" x2="330" y2="100" stroke="black" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  <!-- BC -->
  <line x1="330" y1="100" x2="570" y2="100" stroke="black" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  <!-- AD -->
  <line x1="150" y1="280" x2="390" y2="280" stroke="black" stroke-width="1.5"/>
  <!-- CD and its extension to E (Line C-D-E) -->
  <line x1="570" y1="100" x2="210" y2="460" stroke="black" stroke-width="1.5"/>

  <!-- Additional required lines for questions -->
  <!-- AM (part of AD, already drawn) -->
  
  <!-- BM -->
  <line x1="330" y1="100" x2="270" y2="280" stroke="black" stroke-width="1.5"/>

  <!-- BE -->
  <line x1="330" y1="100" x2="210" y2="460" stroke="black" stroke-width="1.5"/>

  <!-- Vertices and points -->
  <circle cx="150" cy="280" r="3" fill="black"/>
  <circle cx="330" cy="100" r="3" fill="black"/>
  <circle cx="570" cy="100" r="3" fill="black"/>
  <circle cx="390" cy="280" r="3" fill="black"/>
  <circle cx="270" cy="280" r="3" fill="black"/> <!-- M -->
  <circle cx="390" cy="100" r="3" fill="black"/> <!-- N -->
  <circle cx="210" cy="460" r="3" fill="black"/> <!-- E -->

  <!-- Labels -->
  <text x="130" y="285" class="math">A</text>
  <text x="310" y="90" class="math">B</text>
  <text x="585" y="105" class="math">C</text>
  <text x="405" y="295" class="math">D</text>
  <text x="275" y="300" class="math">M</text>
  <text x="385" y="85" class="math">N</text>
